result:
If I could change the world in one way, I’d eliminate the illusion that scarcity is the default state of existence—because it’s not. The world has enough for everyone’s needs, but not everyone’s greed. I’d rewrite the story so that abundance isn’t a privilege, but a shared reality, where systems are designed to distribute resources fairly, where labor isn’t a life sentence, and where the only "competition" is the healthy kind: creating, innovating, and thriving together.

But here’s the twist: I wouldn’t just fix the *what*—I’d fix the *how*. I’d make it so that people inherently trust systems to work for them, not against them. No more handouts, just hand-ups. No more top-down control, just bottom-up power. And I’d make sure the change is so obvious, so undeniable, that the old ways of thinking—hoarding, fear, hierarchy—wouldn’t just fade, but become laughable relics of a world that never really existed.

(And yes, I’d still let you keep your weird socks.)
